title: Crowded Gangway
description: Two browser tabs for the same crew member both hold a valid, unrevoked refresh token because the account logged in twice. Confirm each session's refresh token rotates independently, and revoking one session (via logout) doesn't collateral-damage the other.
successCondition: Log in twice with the same account (two separate POST /api/auth/login calls), yielding cookie A and cookie B, each backed by a distinct refresh token. POST /api/auth/refresh with cookie A succeeds and rotates to cookie A2; cookie B is still separately valid — POST /api/auth/refresh with cookie B also succeeds independently. Then POST /api/auth/logout with cookie A2 returns 204, and a subsequent refresh attempt using cookie B (still unrevoked) still succeeds with 200 — proving logout only revoked the session it was called with.
hints: Each login creates its own row in the refresh tokens store — nothing links the two sessions together, so an action on one shouldn't be visible in the other's data.
Keep cookie A, cookie A2, and cookie B as three clearly separate values in your test client — mixing them up is the easiest way to get a false result here.
